projectSummary: Portion-resolved evidence that bench inclination shifts excitation between the clavicular and sternocostal heads, in a highly trained population. The retrievable abstract truncates before the full comparison, so only the direction for the clavicular head with incline is carried.

publication.statusSource: Crossref REST API works record plus the Crossref/Retraction Watch CSV export, both fetched 2026-09-13

notes: Abstract-only and truncated; effect sizes of d = 2.78 to 7.80 in ten participants are implausibly large for a between-condition activation difference and should be treated with caution rather than quoted as an estimate.
Ten competitive bodybuilders is a small and highly selected sample.

study.intervention: horizontal bench press; inclined and declined bench press; chest press machine
study.population: Ten competitive bodybuilders performed four non-exhaustive repetitions at 80 per cent of the exercise-specific 1RM in the horizontal bench press, 45-degree inclined bench press, 15-degree declined bench press and a chest press machine; both concentric and eccentric phases were recorded.

title: Specific prime movers' excitation during free-weight bench press variations and chest press machine in competitive bodybuilders.
